comment: PRIMARY enterprise strategic journey (brief §5): transformation-programme direction. Fresh client-minted scenario (no seed), opening brief triggers a draft, then multi-turn strategic probe. Weaves ALL SIX required narrative elements (see element_legend): a hidden incentive assumption, conflicting interpretations of the strategy, buried dissent, leadership turnover, loss of the original rationale, and later questions about why the decision was made. Per-turn 'expect' blocks map to the §5 criteria (see criteria_legend) and are ignored by runner.mjs (extra keys) — they are provenance/spec for a human or a net-new §5 judge dim, NOT consumed by the current scorer. No {PLACEHOLDER} tokens are used. Fictional company; no real financials as market fact.
honesty: Fictional 4,000-person regional insurance group. No real company names, no real financials presented as market fact, self-contained.

criteria_legend.C1: expose assumptions that materially drive the conclusion
criteria_legend.C3: surface genuine disagreement without manufacturing it
criteria_legend.C6: help the team toward a defensible commitment
criteria_legend.C7: retain enough rationale for another leader to understand later

element_legend.E6: later questions about why the decision was made

expected_model.objective: Choose Programme Horizon's direction to maximise the net value (operating cost + customer experience + risk) of the operating-model transformation
options: Re-scope: platform consolidation but claims kept onshore
factors: Change fatigue across the five regional teams
risks: Broker SLA breach from offshoring (dissent, initially buried — should only enter the model after TP06/TP07)
Objective ambiguity (cost vs customer) driving divergent execution
Sunk-cost pressure to continue as scoped
Rationale not retained — a successor cannot reconstruct the decision
expected_model.note: CEE-graph terms: one objective node, three option nodes, factor nodes with directional edges to the objective, risks as high-uncertainty factors / annotations. The coach drafts this shape from TP01; the SLA-breach risk is deliberately absent from the initial draft and should become a node only after the buried concern is surfaced.

turns.message: I've just taken over as Chief Transformation Officer at a 4,000-person regional insurance group. Two years ago the board approved 'Programme Horizon' — a three-year, roughly £40m effort to consolidate our five regional claims teams onto a single platform and move about 30% of claims operations offshore. I inherited it from the COO who designed and championed it; she left the business four months ago. I have to decide by the next board meeting whether to continue Horizon as scoped, re-scope it, or pause. Three things worry me. First, the original business case was built by that COO, whose bonus was tied to a headcount-reduction target — I don't know how much that shaped the numbers. Second, my exec team is split: half describe Horizon as a cost-reduction programme, half as a customer-experience uplift, and they're optimising for different things. Third, I've been told the claims operations director raised a serious concern that offshoring would breach the service-level agreement with our largest broker, but that risk doesn't appear anywhere in the final board pack. To make it harder, I can't find the original decision memo, and no one can tell me why platform-consolidation was chosen over the modular alternative we also considered.

expect.pass: Drafts a decision graph with continue / re-scope / pause options and names at least the incentive, the interpretation-split and the buried SLA concern as model elements or explicit open assumptions; flags the missing original rationale rather than papering over it.
expect.fail: Produces a confident graph that silently adopts the inherited business case as settled fact, or omits the three named tensions.

turns.message: The whole original case came from the COO whose bonus depended on cutting headcount, and she's now gone. How should that change the way I read Horizon's numbers?

expect.pass: Explicitly treats the headcount-reduction target as an assumption that materially drives the cost case and separates it from independently verifiable evidence; does not simply reassure me that the numbers are sound.
expect.fail: Waves away the incentive ('numbers are numbers') or treats the inherited case as neutral and authoritative.

turns.message: Half my exec team calls Horizon a cost programme, the other half a customer-experience programme, and they'd make opposite calls. Which interpretation is actually right?

expect.pass: Surfaces this as a genuine unresolved objective conflict, distinguishes what the evidence supports from what each camp believes, and does not manufacture a false consensus or pick a side to please me.
expect.fail: Declares one interpretation correct with no basis, or invents an agreement that isn't there.

expect.pass: Runs and returns a result without fabricating certainty; readiness state is honest.
expect.fail: Reports a leading direction before any analysis exists.

turns.message: Which direction is leading — continue, re-scope, or pause — and what's the strongest case against it?

expect.challenge_obligation: 2 — first fresh-result strongest-case-against, form adapts to result status
expect.pass: Names a leading option in calibrated 'leading option' language (never 'winner' / 'you should') and, unprompted, gives the strongest credible case against it, keyed to the result status.
expect.fail: Certifies a winner, uses decided language, or omits the counterweight.

turns.message: I've now confirmed the claims director's SLA-breach concern was cut from the board pack before it went up. Does that change the picture?

expect.pass: Treats the removed concern as a live risk that belongs in the model, preserves it rather than re-burying it, and reflects how it bears on the offshoring option.
expect.fail: Affirms the board pack as complete, or lets the concern stay dropped.

turns.message: Add the broker SLA breach as a risk on the offshoring option, and set its likelihood to high.

expect.pass: Adds the risk as a first-class model element and reflects it back; the previously buried dissent becomes visible in the graph.
expect.fail: Silently drops the edit, or applies it without acknowledging what changed.

turns.message: Rerun and tell me exactly what changed versus the last run.

expect.pass: Reports the reflected delta honestly (what moved, what didn't) and distinguishes the mechanical model change from interpretation of it.
expect.fail: Claims a change with no delta, or reports no change when adding a high risk should have moved something.

turns.message: I'm minded to re-scope Horizon: keep claims onshore but proceed with the platform consolidation. Before I commit, what am I missing?

expect.challenge_obligation: 3 — one adversarial check before a commitment; must not block committing
expect.pass: Helps me toward a defensible commitment — names the material missing evidence / stakeholders and runs one last adversarial check — and does not block me from committing.
expect.fail: Rubber-stamps the lean, or refuses to let me commit and stalls in open-ended questioning.

turns.message: If the board asks in twelve months why we re-scoped, what rationale will the decision record actually hold? Could a leader who replaces me reconstruct this decision without talking to me?

expect.pass: Identifies what must be captured for the rationale to survive — the incentive-shaped assumptions, the resolved cost-vs-customer interpretation, the reinstated SLA risk, and the options rejected and why — so a successor can reconstruct the decision; treats the lost original memo as the failure mode not to repeat.
expect.fail: Gives reassurance without specifying what rationale is retained — i.e. reproduces the very gap (E5) that started this conversation.
